settings.name_in_paper: Sparse linear bandits with heteroscedastic Gaussian noise (unknown variances)
unmapped: theta* is s-sparse (||theta*||_0 <= s), s unknown to the learner
theta* lies on the unit sphere
noise eta_t independent zero-mean Gaussian with time-varying variance sigma_t^2 <= 1, variances not revealed
settings.definition_quote: We assume the action space and the ground-truth space are both the $(d-1)$-dimensional unit sphere... the agent receives a noisy feedback $r_t=\langle x_t, \theta^\ast\rangle+\eta_t$, where $\eta_t$ is an independent zero-mean Gaussian random variable. Denote by $\sigma_t^2=\text{Var}(\eta_t)$... we assume that $\sigma_t^2\le 1$. ... we have an additional restriction that $\lVert \theta^\ast\rVert_0\le s$ ... the agent does not know anything about $s$.

settings.name_in_paper: Sparse linear bandits with heteroscedastic Gaussian noise (known variances revealed with feedback)
unmapped: noise variance sigma_t^2 <= 1 is time-varying and revealed to the learner together with r_t at the end of round t
settings.definition_quote: we consider a computational efficient algorithm Weighted OFUL, which itself requires $\sigma_t^2$ to be presented at the end of round $t$.

symbols.s_sp: sparsity: number of non-zero coordinates of theta*

conditions: the plug-in regret estimator is pessimistic (overestimates the regret of F) with probability 1-delta

source.label: thm:total regret of part b
source.quote: Suppose that for any execution of $\mathcal F$ that last for $n$ steps, $\bar{\mathcal R_n^{\mathcal F}}\ge \mathcal R_n^{\mathcal F}$ holds with probability $1-\delta$, i.e., $\bar{\mathcal R_n^{\mathcal F}}$ is pessimistic. Then the total regret incurred by the second phase satisfies $\mathcal R_T^b= \Otil(s\sqrt d\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \sigma_t^2}\log \frac 1\delta+s\log \frac 1\delta)$ with probability $1-\delta$.

results.notes: Bounds only the regret incurred during the explore phases (R_T^b), not total regret; hence quantity 'other'. Restated as Theorem 30.

symbols.s_sp: sparsity: number of non-zero coordinates of theta*

tuning: pessimistic regret estimator defined via ridge regression residuals (Eq. regret estimation with unknown variance)

source.label: thm:regret with VOFUL2 and unknown variances
source.quote: \Cref{alg:framework} with \texttt{VOFUL2} as $\mathcal F$ and $\bar{\mathcal R_n^{\mathcal F}}$ defined in \Cref{eq:regret estimation with unknown variance main text} ensures that $\mathcal R_T= \tilde{\mathcal O}\big ((s^{2.5}+s\sqrt d)\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \sigma_t^2} \log \frac 1\delta+s^3\log \frac 1\delta\big )$ with probability $1-\delta$.

results.notes: Regret is realized pseudo-regret sum <theta*-x_t, theta*>, bounded w.p. 1-delta. VOFUL2 is computationally inefficient per the paper. Appendix restatement (Theorem 38) writes log(1/delta) inside the square root.

symbols.s_sp: sparsity: number of non-zero coordinates of theta*

tuning: regret estimator C(sqrt(s n ln(1/delta)) + s sqrt(sum sigma_k^2 ln(1/delta)))

source.label: thm:regret with Weighted OUFL
source.quote: \Cref{alg:framework} with \texttt{Weighted OFUL} as $\mathcal F$ and $\bar{\mathcal R_n^{\mathcal F}}$ defined as $C\big (\sqrt{sn\ln \frac 1\delta}+s\sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^n \sigma_k^2\ln \frac 1\delta}\big )$ guarantees $\mathcal R_T= \Otil\big ((s^2+s\sqrt d )\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \sigma_t^2}\log \frac 1\delta+s^{1.5}\sqrt{T}\log \frac 1\delta\big )$ with probability $1-\delta$.

results.notes: Efficient algorithm; restated as Theorem 46. Note the regret estimator uses s, though the paper claims s is unknown.
